findings.text: Parallel: the text sets two inner components side by side as near-equivalents, as in a clean heart and a right spirit (Psa 51:10).

findings.text: Wholeness: the text adds terms to name the whole person: all your heart and all your soul (Deu 6:5); spirit and soul and body (1 Th 5:23).
Unity and division: one heart, one soul, one flesh; a double heart (Psa 86:11; Psa 12:2; Gal 5:17).
Containment: the heart as the innermost place things are put: the Spirit in our hearts (Gal 4:6); law, idols and eternity in the heart.
Cause and effect: an inner state and the body, face, food and senses answer each other: a crushed spirit dries up the bones (Pro 17:22); bread strengthens the heart.
Opposition: flesh against Spirit in the NT (Gal 5:16-17); in the OT flesh is frail, not hostile (Isa 31:3).
Shared between persons: souls knit, hearts joined or stolen, spirit passed on (1 Sam 18:1; 2 Sam 15:6; 2 Kgs 2:9).

findings.text: Parted at death: dust to earth, spirit to God, soul to Sheol or delivered (Eccl 12:7; Gen 35:18).
The components come apart sharply only at death, in Paul's flesh and Spirit contrast, in Heb 4:12 (the division of soul and of spirit) and in 1 Cor 14:14 (spirit and mind in prayer).
